bracket: [Textbook answer-key error, and the key contradicts itself inside one sentence: it reads "Except \(\text{Sc}^{3+}\), all others will be coloured in aqueous solution because of incompletely filled 3d-orbitals". The REASON it gives is exactly what excludes \(\text{Cu}^{+}\), which its scope "all others" includes — \(\text{Cu}^{+}\) is \(3d^{10}\), a completely filled set with no vacancy, so no \(d\)-\(d\) transition is possible and the ion is colourless. It should read "Except \(\text{Sc}^{3+}\) AND \(\text{Cu}^{+}\)". Two further confirmations come from the chapter itself: §4.3.10 defines the colour as promotion of an electron INTO a higher \(d\) orbital, impossible for \(d^{10}\); and its own Table 4.8 lists every \(d^0\) and \(d^{10}\) species as colourless, including \(3d^{10}\) \(\text{Zn}^{2+}\), which is \(\text{Cu}^{+}\)'s exact configuration.]
